queue.title: A Figure Without Methodology Is Not Information
queue.content:
A financial indicator published without explaining its calculation methodology is worth less than it appears. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

A financial indicator published without a clear explanation of how it was calculated is worth less than it appears at first glance.

A financial indicator published without a clear explanation of how it was calculated is worth less than it appears at first glance.

Publishing a key financial indicator without an accompanying explanation of the calculation methodology leaves room for differing interpretations and, ultimately, reduces the credibility of the figure itself, however accurate it may be on its own.

When a short explanation of the data source and calculation method accompanies each key indicator, the reader is able to judge the reliability of the information rather than simply taking it on faith.

queue.title: A Few Accurate Indicators Are Worth More Than Many Approximate Ones
queue.content:
A report with fifty superficial metrics rarely paints a clearer picture than five well-chosen, accurately measured indicators. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

A report with fifty superficial metrics rarely gives a better picture than five well-chosen, accurately measured indicators.

A report with fifty superficial metrics rarely gives a better picture than five well-chosen, accurately measured indicators.

The number of tracked indicators is often mistakenly equated with the quality of oversight, while a smaller number of carefully chosen and reliably measured metrics usually gives a clearer picture of the real state of a business. GNK ASG d.o.o. deliberately limits the number of key indicators in public reporting precisely so each one retains real weight and verifiability.

When the number of indicators is deliberately limited, it's also easier to ensure each one is genuinely measured accurately and reviewed regularly, rather than just updated occasionally.
